_doc.description: Shared conformance vectors for the bench derived-signal grammar (docs/api/bench-view.md section 4). Both evaluators (packages/api/.../livebench/view/expression.py and apps/desktop/.../features/bench/view/expression.ts) must pass every case.

encoding.numbers: Non-finite numbers are JSON strings: "NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity". They may appear as input values, input timestamps and expected values. Expected outputs only ever contain finite numbers or "NaN".
encoding.positions: position/length are 0-based offsets in Unicode code points of the expression.
encoding.parse: accept: {node_count, depth, refs (distinct, first-appearance order)}; reject: {code, position, length}.
encoding.evaluate: inputs: [{device_id, signal, samples: [[t, v], ...]}] in arrival order, or ramp: {count, dt, dv} meaning sample i = [i*dt, i*dv]. expected: [[t, v], ...] (full output), or expected_count + expected_head/expected_tail (first/last outputs). Zero-reference (constant) expressions: inputs is [] and the case carries timestamps: [t, ...] (the time base; the primary drop rule applies) or at: t (no time base: one sample at t). A case with references may carry timestamps to prove they are ignored.
encoding.tolerance: relative 1e-9 (a == b or |a-b| <= 1e-9 * max(|a|,|b|)); NaN equals NaN; timestamps compare with the same tolerance.

clarifications.depth: Root = 1. A parenthesised group is not a node (node_count) but adds one depth level, so '((((...' fails at the 12th '(' (docs/architecture/bench-view.md section 2). too_deep is raised while descending (the opening '(', '-' or function name that enters level 13) or when a node is built whose height exceeds 12 (span = that node).
clarifications.check_order: too_long (before lexing); then lexical errors over the whole text (syntax: unexpected char / unterminated string; non_finite_literal); then parse errors in parse order (syntax, unknown_function, bad_ref, too_deep, arity, non_constant_param, param_range, too_many_nodes, too_many_refs - call checks run when the call's ')' is consumed). A zero-reference expression is accepted as a constant signal (no_signal was removed by the SOLUSDEV-319 constant-derived-signals amendment).
clarifications.spans: syntax: the offending token (length 0 at end of input; an unterminated string spans to the end); bad_ref: the string literal with quotes; unknown_function: the identifier; arity: the whole call; non_constant_param/param_range: the argument (param_range for scale in_lo == in_hi: the in_hi argument); too_many_nodes: the node whose construction made 65; too_many_refs: the sig(...) introducing the 9th ref.
clarifications.constants: A constant is a number literal or '-' directly followed by one (no parentheses, no double minus).
clarifications.empty_call: abs() does not match the grammar (call needs >= 1 argument): syntax.
clarifications.references: Every reference (not only the primary) drops samples whose timestamp is not strictly greater than the previous accepted one, or is non-finite. Non-finite input values read as NaN. Primary values come from the same hold lookup (age 0 at its own timestamps).
clarifications.lowpass: dt is measured from the last finite sample the filter consumed; the gap check uses consecutive output timestamps.
clarifications.formulas: scale = out_lo + (x - in_lo) * (out_hi - out_lo) / (in_hi - in_lo); trapezoid term = (t_i - t_prev) * (x_i + x_prev) / 2; lowpass RC = 1 / (2 * pi * fc); min/max fold left with < / >.
clarifications.constant_signals: An expression with zero references is a constant signal (bench-view.md section 4.6): refs []; outputs at the supplied time base (timestamps) or one sample at 'at'; filters run on that time base per section 4.5.
